# Story 16 — Escalate to a human agent

---

## Prerequisites

- Story 14 completed: `POST /api/v1/conversations` creates a `Conversation` with `status: "ai_handling"`, `assignedAgent: null`, and Socket.io wiring for `conversation:join`/`conversation:message` is in place (see `backend/src/routes/conversation.routes.ts` line 12 and `backend/src/sockets/chat.socket.ts` lines 67–174).
- Story 15 completed: the AI branch fires from the `conversation:message` handler *only when* `conversation.status === "ai_handling"` (see `backend/src/sockets/chat.socket.ts` line 139) — that guard is the hinge this story flips.
- Story 17 (auto-assign an escalated chat) is the immediately-following story and consumes the `status: "escalated"` flag set here. **Do not** implement any agent-assignment logic in this story.
- Story 18 (agent-side reply UI) will render escalated conversations for staff — do not touch agent-side surfaces here.

---

## Story Goal

Give the customer a first-class way to say "talk to a human" from inside the live chat, and have that action:

1. Flip the conversation's `status` to `"escalated"` so it stops receiving AI replies and becomes eligible for Story 17's auto-assignment queue.
2. Emit a real-time signal on the conversation room so the customer's UI immediately shows an "escalated — waiting for an agent" state.
3. Leave the full prior AI/customer message history intact (no message deletion, no separate transcript) so the human agent who later joins (Stories 17/18) reads the same `Message` documents already persisted.

**Out of scope:** picking or notifying an agent, agent-facing UI, closing the conversation. Only the flag + queue signal.

## Product rules (from story)

- **Trigger transport:** use a Socket.io event `conversation:escalate` (payload `{ conversationId }`), **not** a REST endpoint. Rationale: `conversation:message` is already the customer's only real-time channel into the conversation; a socket event keeps the escalate action authenticated the same way (`socket.data.user`), authorised the same way (`isAuthorizedOnConversation`), and delivered/broadcast on the same connection. This matches the "don't introduce a second parallel transport for a very similar concern without reason" note in the intake.
- **REST stub disposition:** delete the placeholder `router.post("/:id/escalate", …)` at `backend/src/routes/conversation.routes.ts` lines 32–36 and its regression test at `backend/tests/routes/conversation.routes.test.ts` lines 71–77. Do not leave a 501 route hanging.
- **Idempotent:** escalating a conversation that is already `"escalated"` or `"with_agent"` is a no-op success (no error emitted, no re-broadcast).
- **Terminal:** escalating a `"resolved"` conversation is rejected with the same shape as the existing "This conversation is closed" error (see `chat.socket.ts` line 119).
- **Authorisation:** only the conversation's own `customer` may escalate. Agents/admins never trigger escalation on behalf of the customer in this story. Reuse `isAuthorizedOnConversation` and additionally check `socket.data.user.id === String(conversation.customer)`.
- **AI stops:** because the AI branch is gated on `conversation.status === "ai_handling"` (line 139), setting status to `"escalated"` naturally halts AI replies with no other change.
- **History preserved:** do not delete, hide, or archive any `Message` documents. Do not write a synthetic "conversation escalated" message in this story (the room-level `conversation:escalated` broadcast is enough for the UI; a system-message could be added later without breaking this contract).

## Backend Tasks

### 1 — Add the escalate payload schema

**File:** `backend/src/validation/conversation.schema.ts`

Add, matching the `conversationMessagePayloadSchema` pattern at lines 10–13:

```ts
export const conversationEscalatePayloadSchema = z.object({
  conversationId: objectIdSchema("Invalid conversation id"),
});
```

Export it alongside the existing schemas. No other changes in this file.

### 2 — Wire the `conversation:escalate` socket handler

**File:** `backend/src/sockets/chat.socket.ts`

1. Import the new schema at the top of the file next to the existing `conversationMessagePayloadSchema` import (line 7).
2. Inside the `io.on("connection", …)` block (starts line 67), **after** the `conversation:message` handler (ends line 169) and **before** the `disconnect` handler (line 171), add a new handler:

   ```ts
   socket.on("conversation:escalate", async (payload: { conversationId: string }) => {
     const parsed = conversationEscalatePayloadSchema.safeParse(payload);
     if (!parsed.success) {
       socket.emit("conversation:error", { error: parsed.error.issues[0]?.message ?? "Invalid escalate payload" });
       return;
     }
     const { conversationId } = parsed.data;

     const conversation = await Conversation.findById(conversationId);
     if (!conversation) {
       socket.emit("conversation:error", { error: "Conversation not found" });
       return;
     }

     // Customer-only: agents never escalate on the customer's behalf in this story.
     if (socket.data.user.id !== String(conversation.customer)) {
       socket.emit("conversation:error", { error: "You do not have permission to escalate this conversation" });
       return;
     }

     if (conversation.status === "resolved") {
       socket.emit("conversation:error", { error: "This conversation is closed" });
       return;
     }

     // Idempotent: already-escalated / already-with-agent is a no-op success.
     if (conversation.status === "escalated" || conversation.status === "with_agent") {
       socket.emit("conversation:escalated", { conversationId, status: conversation.status });
       return;
     }

     conversation.status = "escalated";
     await conversation.save();

     io.to(`conversation:${conversationId}`).emit("conversation:escalated", {
       conversationId,
       status: "escalated",
     });
   });
   ```

3. **Do not** modify the `conversation:message` handler's Story 15 guard at line 139 — flipping `status` to `"escalated"` naturally disables the AI branch on the next customer message.

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **Missing/invalid `conversationId` payload** → `conversation:error` with the zod message (validated by `conversationEscalatePayloadSchema` from Task 1, enforced in `chat.socket.ts` handler from Task 2).
- **Non-existent conversation id (valid ObjectId shape but no doc)** → `conversation:error` `"Conversation not found"` (Task 2, first `findById` branch).
- **Non-customer caller (agent/admin token, or a different customer's socket)** → `conversation:error` `"You do not have permission to escalate this conversation"` (Task 2, customer check). Explicitly stricter than `isAuthorizedOnConversation` because that helper allows the `assignedAgent` too.
- **Conversation already `"resolved"`** → `conversation:error` `"This conversation is closed"` (Task 2). Mirrors `chat.socket.ts` line 118–120.
- **Conversation already `"escalated"` or `"with_agent"`** → no error, re-emit `conversation:escalated` to the caller only so a reconnecting client can re-sync UI state (Task 2, idempotent branch).
- **Customer sends another message after escalation** → persisted normally by the existing `conversation:message` handler; the AI branch (line 139) is skipped because status is no longer `"ai_handling"`. **Verify** in tests.
- **Concurrent escalate + message race** → both `save`/`create` operations touch different documents; the worst case is that one extra AI reply fires just before the status flip lands. Acceptable for this story; do not add a lock. Note this in a code comment above the handler.
- **DB save failure on `conversation.save()`** → uncaught; falls to socket.io's default error path. Do not silently swallow. (No try/catch added — matches the rest of the handlers in this file which also don't wrap DB writes.)
- **Client reconnects after escalation** → on `conversation:join` (existing handler lines 72–92), the client already re-reads the conversation. Frontend should also emit `conversation:escalate` again on reconnect *only if* it believes it hasn't been acknowledged — the idempotent branch above covers this. **Do not** auto-emit on every reconnect; the user's initial action is what matters.
- **Escalate emitted before `conversation:joined`** → the socket-level handler doesn't require room membership, so the DB update lands, but the room broadcast reaches nobody. Acceptable — the caller still gets the direct emit from the idempotent branch on their next reconnect join. Document with an inline comment.

## Migration / Rollback

- **No schema migration required.** `ConversationStatus` already includes `"escalated"` (`backend/src/models/Conversation.ts` line 3, enum line 31); existing conversations continue to default to `"ai_handling"`.
- **Rollback:** revert this story's diff. Any conversation left in `status: "escalated"` before rollback would still be valid data (already in the enum) but would not be picked up by any Story 17 code (which won't exist yet after rollback), so it would simply sit idle — no data corruption, no cleanup required. Optionally: `db.conversations.updateMany({ status: "escalated" }, { $set: { status: "ai_handling" } })` to resume AI handling on those chats.

6. **Regression — idempotence:** double-click "Talk to a human" (or replay the emit via devtools) → no duplicate `conversation:escalated` broadcast in the network tab; no server error.
